readings.title: A Voice in the Wilderness
readings.subtitle: Prepare the Way of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Isaiah 40:1] <dq>“Comfort, comfort <dn>My</dn> people!”</dq> says your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] <dq>“Speak to the heart of Yerushalayim, and cry out to her, that her hard service is completed, that her crookedness is pardoned, that she has received from the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> double for all her sins.”</dq> [3] The voice of one crying in the wilderness, “Prepare the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; make straight in the desert a highway for our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [4] “Let every valley be raised, and every mountain and hill made low. And the steep ground shall become level, and the rough places smooth. [5] “And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see it. For the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.” [6] The voice said, “Cry out!” and he said, “What do <dn>I</dn> cry?” “All flesh is grass, and all its loving-commitment is like the flower of the field. [7] “Grass shall wither, the flower shall fade, when the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blown on it! Truly the people is grass! [8] “Grass shall wither, the flower shall fade, but the Word of our <dn>Elohim</dn> stands forever.” [9] You who bring good news to Tsiyon, get up into the high mountain. You who bring good news to Yerushalayim, lift up your voice with strength, lift it up, be not afraid. Say to the cities of Yehuḏah, “See <dn>את</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>!” [10] See, the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> comes with strength, and <dn>His</dn> arm rules for <dn>Him</dn>. See, <dn>His</dn> reward is with <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> recompense before <dn>Him</dn>. [11] <dn>He</dn> feeds <dn>His</dn> flock like a shepherd, <dn>He</dn> gathers the lambs with <dn>His</dn> arm, and carries them in <dn>His</dn> bosom, gently leading those who are with young.

readings.title: Who Has Measured the Heavens?
readings.subtitle: The Futility of Idols
readings.text: [Isaiah 40:12] Who has measured the waters in the hollow of <dn>his</dn> hand, and measured <dn>את</dn> the heavens with a span, and contained the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance? [13] Who has meted out <dn>את</dn> the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, or as <dn>His</dn> counsellor taught <dn>Him</dn>? [14] With whom did <dn>He</dn> take counsel, and who instructed <dn>Him</dn>, and taught <dn>Him</dn> in the path of right-ruling? Who taught <dn>Him</dn> knowledge, and showed <dn>Him</dn> the way of understanding? [15] See, nations are as a drop in a bucket, and are reckoned as dust on the balance. See, <dn>He</dn> lifts up isles as fine dust. [16] And Leḇanon is not enough to burn, nor its beasts enough for an ascending offering. [17] All nations before <dn>Him</dn> are as a non-entity, and they are reckoned by <dn>Him</dn> as less than a speck, and emptiness. [18] And to whom would you liken <dn>Ěl</dn>? And what likeness would you compare to <dn>Him</dn>? [19] The workman moulds a graven image, and the goldsmith overspreads it with gold, and the silversmith casts silver chains. [20] He who is too poor for such an offering chooses a tree that does not rot. He seeks for himself a skilled craftsman to prepare a carved image that does not totter.

readings.title: The Everlasting Elohim
readings.subtitle: He Gives Power to the Faint
readings.text: [Isaiah 40:21] Did you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth? [22] It is <dn>He</dn> who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers, who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in, [23] who brings princes to naught, shall make the rulers of the earth as emptiness. [24] Hardly have they been planted, hardly have they been sown, hardly has their stock taken root in the earth, when <dn>He</dn> shall blow on them and they wither, and a whirlwind take them away like stubble. [25] <dq>“And to whom then do you liken <dn>Me</dn>, or to whom am <dn>I</dn> compared?”</dq> says the Set-apart One. [26] Lift up your eyes on high and see. Who has created these? <dn>He</dn> is bringing out their host by number, <dn>He</dn> calls them all by name, by the greatness of ability and potent of power, a man is not lacking. [27] Why do you say, O Ya‛aqoḇ, and speak, O Yisra’ěl, “My way is hidden from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and my rights are overlooked by my <dn>Elohim</dn>”? [28] Did you not know? Have you not heard? The everlasting <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Creator of the ends of the earth, neither faints nor is weary. <dn>His</dn> understanding is unsearchable. [29] <dn>He</dn> gives power to the faint, and to those who have no might <dn>He</dn> increases strength. [30] Even youths shall faint and be weary, and young men stumble and fall, [31] but those who wait on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> renew their strength, they raise up the wing like eagles, they run and are not weary, they walk and do not faint.

readings.title: The Righteous One from the East
readings.subtitle: A Challenge to the Coastlands
readings.text: [Isaiah 41:1] <dq>“Be silent before <dn>Me</dn>, you coastlands, and let peoples renew their power! Let them come near, then let them speak. Let us come together for right-ruling.</dq> [2] <dq>“Who raised up the righteous one from the east, called him to <dn>His</dn> foot, gave the nations before him, and made sovereigns submit to him? <dn>He</dn> gave them as the dust to his sword, as driven stubble to his bow.</dq> [3] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> pursued them, passed over in safety, by a path that he had not gone with his feet.</dq> [4] <dq>“Who has performed and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? ‘<dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, am the first, and with the last <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>.’ ”</dq> [5] Coastlands see it and fear, the ends of the earth are afraid – they draw near and come. [6] Everyone helps his neighbour, and says to his brother, “Be strong!” [7] And the craftsman strengthens the goldsmith. He who smooths with the hammer inspires him who strikes the anvil, saying of the joining, “It is good.” And he strengthens it with nails, so it does not totter.

readings.title: Fear Not, My Servant
readings.subtitle: I Will Uphold You
readings.text: [Isaiah 41:8] <dq>“But you, Yisra’ěl, are <dn>My</dn> servant, Ya‛aqoḇ, whom <dn>I</dn> have chosen, the descendants of Aḇraham who loved <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [9] <dq>whom <dn>I</dn> have strengthened from the ends of the earth, and called from its farthest parts, and said to You, ‘You are <dn>My</dn> servant, <dn>I</dn> have chosen you and have not rejected you.</dq> [10] <dq>Do not fear, for <dn>I</dn> am with you. Do not look around, for <dn>I</dn> am your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> shall fortify you, <dn>I</dn> shall also help you, <dn>I</dn> shall also uphold you with the right hand of <dn>My</dn> righteousness.’</dq> [11] <dq>“See, all those who raged against you are ashamed and blush, they are as non-existent. And the men who strive with you perish.</dq> [12] <dq>“You seek them but do not find them, those who struggle with you. Those who fight you are as non-existent, as naught.</dq> [13] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, am strengthening your right hand, saying to you, ‘Do not fear, <dn>I</dn> shall help you.’</dq> [14] <dq>“Do not fear, you worm Ya‛aqoḇ, you men of Yisra’ěl! <dn>I</dn> shall help you,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and your Redeemer, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl. [15] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> shall make you into a new threshing sledge with sharp teeth, let you thresh mountains and beat them small, and make hills like chaff.</dq> [16] <dq>“You winnow them, the wind lifts them up, and the whirlwind scatters them; but you, you rejoice in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and boast in the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.</dq>

readings.title: Water in the Wilderness
readings.subtitle: The Hand of YeHoVaH Revealed
readings.text: [Isaiah 41:17] <dq>“When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongues have failed for thirst, <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do answer them; <dn>I</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, do not forsake them.</dq> [18] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> open rivers on bare hills, and fountains in the midst of valleys; <dn>I</dn> make a wilderness become a pool of water, and a dry land springs of water.</dq> [19] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> set in the wilderness cedar, acacia and myrtle and oil tree; <dn>I</dn> place in the desert cypress, pine and box tree together.</dq> [20] <dq>“So that they see and know, and consider and understand together, that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done this, and the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl has created it.</dq>

readings.title: The Impotence of Idols
readings.subtitle: Who Can Declare What is to Come?
readings.text: [Isaiah 41:21] <dq>“Present your case,”</dq> says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Let your strong ones come near,”</dq> says the Sovereign of Ya‛aqoḇ. [22] <dq>“Let them draw near and declare to us what is going to take place; let them declare <dn>את</dn> the former events, what they were, and we consider them, and know the latter end of them; or announce to us what is coming.</dq> [23] <dq>“Declare the events that are going to come hereafter, and we know that you are mighty ones; yes, do good or do evil, and let us be amazed and see it together.</dq> [24] <dq>“See, you are of naught, and your work a breath; he who chooses you is an abomination.</dq> [25] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have stirred up one from the north, and he comes; from the rising of the sun he calls on <dn>My</dn> Name. And he comes against princes as though mortar, as the potter treads clay.</dq> [26] <dq>“Who has declared from the beginning, and we know? and former times, and we say, ‘<dn>He</dn> is righteous’? No, no one is declaring; no, no one is proclaiming; no, no one is hearing your words.</dq> [27] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> who is First said to Tsiyon, ‘See, see them!’ And to Yerushalayim <dn>I</dn> give one who brings good news.</dq> [28] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> see that there is no man, and of these, there is no counsellor, who, when <dn>I</dn> ask of them, answers a word.</dq> [29] <dq>“See, all of them are useless, their works are naught, their moulded images are wind and confusion.</dq>

readings.title: My Chosen One, My Delight
readings.subtitle: A Covenant and a Light to the Nations
readings.text: [Isaiah 42:1] <dq>“See, <dn>My</dn> Servant whom <dn>I</dn> uphold, <dn>My</dn> Chosen One <dn>My</dn> being has delighted in! <dn>I</dn> have put <dn>My</dn> Spirit upon <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>He</dn> brings forth right-ruling to the nations.</dq> [2] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> does not cry out, nor lifts up <dn>His</dn> voice, nor causes <dn>His</dn> voice to be heard in the street.</dq> [3] <dq>“A crushed reed <dn>He</dn> does not break, and smoking flax <dn>He</dn> does not quench. <dn>He</dn> brings forth right-ruling in accordance with truth.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> does not become weak or crushed, until <dn>He</dn> has established right-ruling in the earth. And the coastlands wait for <dn>His</dn> Torah.”</dq> [5] Thus said the <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread forth the earth and that which comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it, and spirit to those who walk on it: [6] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have called You in righteousness, and <dn>I</dn> strengthen Your hand and guard You, and give You for a covenant to a people, for a light to the nations,</dq> [7] <dq>to open blind eyes, to bring out prisoners from the prison, those who sit in darkness from the prison house.</dq> [8] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that is <dn>My</dn> Name, and <dn>My</dn> esteem <dn>I</dn> do not give to another, nor <dn>My</dn> praise to idols.</dq> [9] <dq>“See, the former predictions have come, and new ones <dn>I</dn> am declaring; before they spring forth <dn>I</dn> let you hear them.”</dq>

readings.title: A New Song of Praise
readings.subtitle: The Warrior Goes Forth
readings.text: [Isaiah 42:10] Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a new song; <dn>His</dn> praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you coastlands and you inhabitants of them! [11] Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voice, the villages where Qěḏar dwells. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing, let them shout from the top of the mountains. [12] Let them give esteem to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and declare <dn>His</dn> praise in the coastlands. [13] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> goes forth like a mighty man. <dn>He</dn> stirs up ardour like a fighter. <dn>He</dn> cries out, yes, shout aloud. Over <dn>His</dn> enemies <dn>He</dn> shows <dn>Himself</dn> mighty. [14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have kept silent from of old, <dn>I</dn> have been still and held <dn>Myself</dn> back. Like a woman in labour <dn>I</dn> now cry out, <dn>I</dn> pant and gasp at once.</dq> [15] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> lay waste mountains and hills, and <dn>I</dn> dry up all their plants. And <dn>I</dn> shall make rivers become coastlands, and <dn>I</dn> dry up pools.</dq> [16] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall lead the blind by a way they have not known – in paths they have not known <dn>I</dn> lead them. <dn>I</dn> make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. These matters <dn>I</dn> shall do for them, and <dn>I</dn> shall not forsake them.</dq> [17] <dq>“Those who trust in idols, who say to the moulded images, ‘You are our mighty ones,’ shall be turned back, utterly ashamed.</dq>

readings.title: A Blind and Deaf People
readings.subtitle: Plundered for Disobedience
readings.text: [Isaiah 42:18] <dq>“Hear, you deaf! And look, you blind, and see.</dq> [19] <dq>“Who is blind but <dn>My</dn> servant, or deaf as <dn>My</dn> messenger whom <dn>I</dn> send? Who is blind as he who is at peace, and blind as servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?</dq> [20] <dq>“You see much, but do not guard; ears are open, but do not hear.”</dq> [21] It has delighted <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for the sake of <dn>His</dn> righteousness, to make the Torah great and esteemed. [22] But this is a people robbed and plundered, all of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prison houses. They have become a prey, with no one to deliver – for plunder, and no one to say, “Restore!” [23] Who among you gives ear to this, pays attention and hears for the time to come? [24] Who gave Ya‛aqoḇ for plunder, and Yisra’ěl to the robbers? Was it not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> against whom we sinned? For they would not walk in <dn>His</dn> ways, and they did not obey <dn>His</dn> Torah! [25] So <dn>He</dn> has poured on him <dn>His</dn> burning displeasure and the strength of battle, and it set him on fire all around, yet he did not understand. And it burned against him, yet he did not take it to heart!

readings.title: Do Not Fear, I Have Redeemed You
readings.subtitle: You Are Precious in My Eyes
readings.text: [Isaiah 43:1] But now, thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Creator, O Ya‛aqoḇ, and <dn>He</dn> who formed you, O Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Do not fear, for <dn>I</dn> have redeemed you. <dn>I</dn> have called you by your name, you are <dn>Mine</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>“When you pass through the waters, <dn>I</dn> am with you; and through rivers, they do not overflow you. When you walk through fire, you are not scorched, and a flame does not burn you.</dq> [3] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, your Saviour; <dn>I</dn> gave Mitsrayim for your ransom, Kush and Seḇa in your place.</dq> [4] <dq>“Since you were precious in <dn>My</dn> eyes, you have been esteemed, and <dn>I</dn> have loved you. And <dn>I</dn> give men in your place, and peoples for your life.</dq> [5] <dq>“Do not fear, for <dn>I</dn> am with you. <dn>I</dn> shall bring your seed from the east, and gather you from the west.</dq> [6] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall say to the north, ‘Give them up!’ And to the south, ‘Do not keep them back!’ Bring <dn>My</dn> sons from afar, and <dn>My</dn> daughters from the ends of the earth –</dq> [7] <dq>all those who are called by <dn>My</dn> Name, whom <dn>I</dn> have created, formed, even made for <dn>My</dn> esteem.”</dq>

readings.title: You Are My Witnesses
readings.subtitle: Besides Me There Is No Saviour
readings.text: [Isaiah 43:8] <dn>He</dn> shall bring out a blind people who have eyes, and deaf ones who have ears. [9] All the nations shall be assembled, and the peoples be gathered. Who among them declares this, and show us former events? Let them give their witnesses, to be declared right; or let them hear and say, “It is truth.” [10] <dq>“You are <dn>My</dn> witnesses,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“And <dn>My</dn> servant whom <dn>I</dn> have chosen, so that you know and believe <dn>Me</dn>, and understand that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>. Before <dn>Me</dn> there was no <dn>Ěl</dn> formed, nor after <dn>Me</dn> there is none.</dq> [11] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and besides <dn>Me</dn> there is no saviour.</dq> [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have declared and saved, and made known, and there was no foreign mighty one among you. And you are <dn>My</dn> witnesses,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn>.</dq> [13] <dq>“Even from the day <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>, and no one delivers out of <dn>My</dn> hand. <dn>I</dn> work, and who turns it back?”</dq>

readings.title: Behold, I Am Doing a New Thing
readings.subtitle: A Way in the Wilderness
readings.text: [Isaiah 43:14] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Redeemer, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“For your sake <dn>I</dn> shall send to Baḇel, and bring them all down as fugitives, even the Kasdim, who rejoice in their ships.</dq> [15] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Set-apart One, Creator of Yisra’ěl, your Sovereign.”</dq> [16] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who makes a way in the sea and a path through the mighty waters, [17] who brings forth the chariot and horse, the army and the power (they lie down together, they do not rise, they have been extinguished, they have been quenched like a wick): [18] <dq>“Do not remember the former events, nor consider the events of old.</dq> [19] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am doing what is new, let it now spring forth. Do you not know it? <dn>I</dn> am even making a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.</dq> [20] <dq>“The beast of the field esteems <dn>Me</dn>, the jackals and the ostriches, because <dn>I</dn> have given waters in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to <dn>My</dn> people, <dn>My</dn> chosen,</dq> [21] <dq>this people <dn>I</dn> have formed for <dn>Myself</dn>, let them relate <dn>My</dn> praise.</dq>

readings.title: You Have Burdened Me With Your Sins
readings.subtitle: I Am He Who Blots Out Transgressions
readings.text: [Isaiah 43:22] <dq>“But you have not called on <dn>Me</dn>, O Ya‛aqoḇ, for you have been weary of <dn>Me</dn>, O Yisra’ěl.</dq> [23] <dq>“You have not brought <dn>Me</dn> the sheep for your ascending offerings, nor have you esteemed <dn>Me</dn> with your slaughterings. <dn>I</dn> have not caused you to serve with grain offerings, nor wearied you with incense.</dq> [24] <dq>“You have not bought <dn>Me</dn> sweet cane with silver, nor have you satisfied <dn>Me</dn> with the fat of your slaughterings. You have only burdened <dn>Me</dn> with your sins, you have wearied <dn>Me</dn> with your crookednesses.</dq> [25] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn> who blots out your transgressions for <dn>My</dn> own sake, and remember your sins no more.</dq> [26] <dq>“Remind <dn>Me</dn>, let us enter into judgment, together; relate, that you might be declared right.</dq> [27] <dq>“Your first father sinned, and your interpreters have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> have profaned the chief ones of the set-apart place, and <dn>I</dn> have delivered up Ya‛aqoḇ to the curse, and Yisra’ěl to scorn.</dq>

readings.title: I Will Pour Out My Spirit
readings.subtitle: They Shall Claim the Name of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Isaiah 44:1] <dq>“But now hear, O Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>My</dn> servant, and Yisra’ěl whom <dn>I</dn> have chosen.</dq> [2] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who made you and formed you from the womb, who helps you, <dq>‘Do not fear, O Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>My</dn> servant, and Yeshurun, whom <dn>I</dn> have chosen.</dq> [3] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> pour water on the thirsty, and floods on the dry ground. <dn>I</dn> pour <dn>My</dn> Spirit on your seed, and <dn>My</dn> blessing on your offspring,</dq> [4] <dq>and they shall spring up among the grass like willows by streams of water.’</dq> [5] <dq>“One says, ‘<dn>I</dn> belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; another calls himself by the name of Ya‛aqoḇ; another writes with his hand, ‘Unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,’ and names himself by the name of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
